svg.title: Allocate Startup Capital Without Buying a Fleet
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-startup-capital-allocation; chart type: stacked_comparison; title: Allocate Startup Capital Without Buying a Fleet; subtitle: Four buckets total $40,000 within the $15,000–$65,000 range.; chapter number: 4; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Numeric values show a $40,000 planning case. Corresponding lean allocations total $15,000 and expanded allocations total $65,000. These are funding envelopes, not automatically deductible expenses or proof of sufficient payment float.; caption: At Base-Case driver settlements of $508,750 annually, smooth 30-day exposure is approximately $41,815 and 45-day exposure is $62,723 before offsets from actual settlement terms.; stages: label: Provider readiness and insurance setup; value: $12,000 planning allocation for service-ready provider onboarding; numeric value: 12000.0; detail: Lean allocation $3,000; expanded allocation $18,000. Fund coverage deposits, credential checks, contract setup, and provider onboarding rather than vehicle purchases.; label: Dispatch and evidence infrastructure; value: $8,000 planning allocation for configured operational tooling; numeric value: 8000.0; detail: Lean allocation $2,000; expanded allocation $12,000. Fund dispatch configuration, barcode equipment, access controls, billing integration, and event-record retention.; label: Commercial setup and pilot preparation; value: $9,000 planning allocation for contracting and service preparation; numeric value: 9000.0; detail: Lean allocation $3,000; expanded allocation $15,000. Fund scoped route discovery, staff preparation, dry runs, payer setup, and account acquisition before live volume.; label: Settlement cash and exception reserve; value: $11,000 planning allocation held for timing and recovery exposure; numeric value: 11000.0; detail: Lean allocation $7,000; expanded allocation $20,000. Size final liquidity from daily settlements and collection lags. This reserve alone cannot fund Base-Case 30-day driver exposure; stage volume or secure additional liquidity.
